title: Geometric-fibre hypotheses and fixed-pair transport for a given comparison system
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Suppose a simultaneous coefficient/pullback datum $S$ [def-fd-pullback-comparison-datum] is given on all noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with $\ell$ invertible, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Write $J_{W,E},J_W$ for its finite and common-stage coefficient equivalences and $b_{h,E}:J_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\simeq F^p_{h,E}J_{T,E}$, $b_h:J_UF_h^s\simeq F_h^pJ_T$ for its comparisons, using the inverses if the datum records the reverse orientation. The operations are the actual framework and PBC completed pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].
Then $X$ is noetherian and finite dimensional, and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring of $X$. The map $g_X$ is a scheme automorphism, with no assumption of $k$-linearity. For $\Lambda=E$ at any finite stage or $\Lambda=\Omega$ at the common stage, put $J=J_{X,\Lambda}$, $F_s=F^s_{g_X,\Lambda}$, $F_p=F^p_{g_X,\Lambda}$ and $b=b_{g_X,\Lambda}$. The formula
$$(K,\theta:F_sK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)\longmapsto(JK,J(\theta)\circ b_K^{-1}),\qquad u\longmapsto J(u)$$
defines an equivalence from the framework Weil-pair category [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] to the category of pairs $(H,\psi:F_pH\simeq H)$ with arrows $v$ satisfying $v\psi=\psi'F_p(v)$. The Hom bijection is exactly the underlying Hom bijection of $J$ restricted to intertwining arrows. These equivalences commute with the finite-stage inclusions into the common-stage pair categories and with scalar extensions, using the specified comparisons in $S$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-geometric-fibre-comparison-hypotheses] to the stated finite-field datum and $X_0$. It supplies Noetherianity, a finite dimension bound, stalkwise invertibility of $\ell$, and the inverse of $g_X$. Hence $X$ and $g_X$ lie in the domain of the supplied datum $S$; no $k$-linearity is needed.

source.place: Final sentence: geometric-fibre hypotheses for the coefficient comparison; returned proof steps 1–3

proof.text: At each finite stage and at the common stage take the equivalence $J$ and comparison $b:JF_s\simeq F_pJ$ from $S$, inverting the recorded comparison when necessary. The framework Weil category is the $F_s$-fixed-pair category by its definition. Apply [lem-fd-fixed-pair-equivalence-transport] with $(F,G)=(F_s,F_p)$. Its object formula is exactly $J(\theta)b_K^{-1}$, its arrow formula is $J(u)$, and its Hom bijection is the specified restriction. This proves all stagewise equivalence clauses. In Lean the supplied comparisons have reverse orientation, so apply fixedPair_equivalence_transport to their symmetries. Transport the finite and common comparisons along finite_functor, sfFinite, pair_functor and sfPair by equality isomorphisms. Their heterogeneous equalities to the supplied comparisons follow by equality elimination. The framework Weil pullbacks differ only in their subsingleton invertibility-instance arguments; equality elimination therefore gives equivalences with exactly the required functors. The finite source categories are explicitly identified by equality of the small coefficient model, field and algebra structures before transporting the functors heterogeneously; this avoids relying on elaborator unfolding of the category implementations.

source.place: Final sentence: transport of Weil structures to the PBC coefficient category; returned proof steps 4–7

proof.text: For each $E\subset L$, the coefficient datum supplies $j:J_LT_s\simeq T_pJ_E$, with its identity and scalar cocycle equations. The pullback datum supplies $r_s,r_p$ and the mixed square in [lem-fd-fixed-pair-mixed-square-lift]. Apply that lemma to obtain the scalar comparison of pair functors with underlying components $j_K$. For finite-to-common inclusions substitute $I_s,I_p,J_X$ for $T_s,T_p,J_L$: the datum's literal-pair component condition gives the same mixed square, so the lemma gives the inclusion comparison too. Its coherence clause preserves the specified identity and cocycle equations. Thus these are the actual comparisons in $S$. For scalar extension, expand the two composite beta components in S.pullback.mixed.comm and replace the finite components using mixed_components. Precompose and postcompose with inverse comparison components to obtain the orientation required by fixedPair_mixedSquare_lift. For inclusions, pair_components identifies the transported common component with the inclusion of the transported finite component. Since every iotaCompFunctorIso component is an identity, this is precisely the mixed-square equation for the inclusion case.
